newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia looks to narrow farm trade gap with HungarY.
newsitem.headline: Croatia looks to narrow farm trade gap with HungarY.

text.p: Croatia's agriculture minister met his Hungarian counterpart in Zagreb on Friday to discuss ways of narrowing the wide farm trade gap between the two countries, state news agency Hina reported.

"The balance shows that Croatia is a big importer of food from Hungary with the ratio 13-to-one in Hungary's favour," Croatian Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic said after talks with Hungary's minister Frigyes Nagy.

Croatia's exports to its neighbour in 1995 totalled $12.5 million against almost $80 million in imports. Last year the gap widened further, with imports rising to almost $99 million while exports were almost halved to $6.8 million.

The trend continued throughout the first quarter of 1997, and Dominikovic expressed fears that current talks on bilateral trade liberalisation within CEFTA (Central European Free Trade Agreement) and Croatia's attempts to join the World Trade Organisation might deepen the problem.
He said Croatia's opportunity to narrow the gap lay in such areas as exports of soy products.
"We discussed a very interesting project concerning soy processing in our Zadar plant and exporting it to Hungary whose annual imports exceed 120,000 tonnes," he said.
Many Croatians regularly travel to Hungary to shop for food because prices are much lower there. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
